items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: And he's the one that promoted the first Bunk recording. Only he wanted me to record Bunk in 1942.

ctx.x: Well, we own all that. Who was Gene Williams? And I never did quite know how he got in the picture and when and when. Was he in the book?

No, he's not. No, he was a student at Columbia University along with Ralph Gleason and a couple other people he knew like Barry Olenov is that his name, the one-time editor of Metronome and Tori Dano was another of his friends there. So I know Gleason's talked about how he started reviewing, Gleason began reviewing records for the Columbia College paper just so he could get free records, I guess, from the companies mostly. And Gene probably did some of that work too. Anyway, Gene started about as soon as he was…
Speaking about Bunk Johnson, how many people were involved really in his coming back? Was there quite a group of people interested in him? I know you played a large part.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1975-02-02
items.q: Gene Williams had heard these records and agreed with me too that at least Bunk showed some possibilities... So Gene's idea was more or less to try to preserve Bunk's tone and Bunk's playing as much as we could get.

ctx.x: Well, you could tell me how American music got started. It started at the beginning.

So anyway, to get back to the point, Gene Williams had heard these records and agreed with me too that at least Bunk showed some possibilities. You couldn't really tell much how he played, both because his lip wasn't in shape and just by himself. The type of trumpet playing that Bunk did, which was a remarkable thing, and yet by itself it wouldn't sound that effective. Bunk was hardly ever on the beat, so if you didn't hear him patting his foot and all there, you could really tell of course where the beat is, but…

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: Gene Williams rushed down there even if he were sick to talk over who should record Bunk

ctx.x: the time even when Lou Waters Band began recording out there in California that's before Bunk made any records at all that's the reason I think I mentioned the last time when Dave Stewart was going to record Bunk and Gene Williams rushed down there even if he were sick to talk over who should record Bunk because Dave had sold so many all the pressings he could make 10,000 he got and sold them all within a few weeks the jukeboxes even of Lou Waters out there and Lou had been playing that stuff for a couple years…
Turk Murphy there then oh yeah
